artists.biography:
Clinic are an English post-punk revival/noise rock band from Liverpool, noted for their often fast-paced, eclectic sound. Their sound is often distinguished by the prominent use of vintage keyboards/organs, most notably the Philips Philicorda, and peculiar off-scale chord progressions.
Clinic was formed in 1997 by Ade Blackburn and Jonathan Hartley following the split of their previous band, Pure Morning. They developed early notoriety for featuring instruments (primarily keyboards/organs) that were acquired at various rummage sales and flea markets. Brian Campbell and Carl Turney joined the band and soon their first EP I.P.C. Subeditors Dictate Our Youth was released on their own Aladdin’s Cave of Golf record label. The EP made John Peel’s Festive 50 at the end of the year and two other self-financed singles followed in 1998.

perplexity.description:
Internal Wrangler is the debut studio album by British indie rock band Clinic, released on 1 May 2000 through Domino Records. The album is a defining work in the post-punk revival and garage rock scenes of the early 2000s, characterized by its raw energy, angular guitar riffs, and the band's distinctive use of keyboards and melodica. Clinic's sound on Internal Wrangler blends elements of new wave, lo-fi rock, and experimental pop, creating a tense, atmospheric quality that set them apart from their contemporaries. The album's brevity—just over 30 minutes—accentuates its intensity, with each track contributing to a cohesive and urgent listening experience.

As Clinic's first full-length release, Internal Wrangler established the band's signature style and laid the groundwork for their subsequent work. It followed their earlier compilation album, which collected their initial EPs, but marked their arrival as a major force in the UK indie scene. The album was well-received by critics for its originality and vitality, earning praise for its inventive songwriting and dynamic performances. Commercially, it reached number 142 on the UK Albums Chart and number 25 on the UK Independent Albums Chart, solidifying Clinic's reputation as a band to watch in the new millennium.
